Construct and dispatch Android intents from Re:T-UI. Usage: $ intent -view <uri> $ intent -activity -a <action> [-d <data>] [-t <mime>] [-p <package>] [-n <package/class>] [--es key value] [--ei key value] [--ez key true|false] $ intent -broadcast -a <action> [-p <package>] [-n <package/class>] [--es key value] $ intent -uri <intent-uri>
Options: -a action, -d data URI, -t MIME type, -p package, -n component. Advanced extras: --es string, --ei integer, --ez boolean. Examples: $ intent -view geo:0,0?q=home $ intent -activity -a android.intent.action.SEND -t text/plain --es android.intent.extra.TEXT standup notes $ intent -broadcast -a net.dinglisch.android.tasker.ACTION_TASK -p net.dinglisch.android.taskerm --es task_name Work

Create and open launcher-native Lua apps.
Usage: $ lua -apps $ lua -new app habit $ lua -app habit $ lua -edit habit $ lua -config habit $ lua -check habit $ lua -info habit $ lua -approve habit $ lua -export habit $ lua -disable habit $ lua -enable habit
Lua apps run inside Re:T-UI, not Termux. They use the same sandbox, prefs, files, permissions, editor, and ui:render layout objects as Lua modules, but open in a focused terminal-styled surface. Inside a Lua app, plain input is sent to on_input(text), and renderer buttons with action/value are sent to on_action(value). Local commands use a colon prefix: :help, :refresh, :restart, :config, :edit, :clear, and :close.

Show and manage Re:T-UI modules.
Usage: $ module -ls $ module -show music $ module -show notifications $ module -show timer $ module -show calendar $ module -show reminder $ module -show notes $ module -show rss $ module -show weather $ module -prompt reminder add $ module -prompt reminder edit $ module -prompt reminder remove $ module -new lua counter $ module -edit counter $ module -config counter $ module -check counter $ module -approve counter $ module -export counter $ module -add server termux:/data/data/com.termux/files/home/retui/server-health.sh $ module -add events termux:/data/data/com.termux/files/home/retui/events.sh $ module -refresh server $ module -rm server $ module -hide music $ module -dock -toggle $ module -dock add server $ module -dock remove music $ module -close
Modules are the single dock/panel category in Re:T-UI. A module can be native, Termux/shell-backed, launcher-backed, or Lua-backed. Built-in modules include music, notifications, timer, calendar, reminder, notes, rss, and weather. Lua modules are edited locally in Re:T-UI, can render native buttons/layouts, and use module -new lua, module -edit, module -config, module -check, and module -approve. Termux modules execute shell scripts and render ::title, ::body, and ::suggest metadata. Suggestion-only Lua scripts remain helpers because they do not render a dock panel.
An empty dock stays empty. To hide or show the dock row live, run module -dock -toggle. You can also turn off show_module_dock in Behavior settings or run config -set show_module_dock false.

-next -> play the next song -previous -> play the previous song -play -> play/pause the player -stop -> stop the player -ls -> list your tracks -select [song] -> play the selected song -info -> get info about the current song -seekto [seconds] -> seek to the selected part of the current song

Safe actions now: output, notify, module_set

-add -> open the RSS setup form -add [ID] [update_time_in_seconds] [url] -> add a new RSS feed. Re:T-UI will try to get new contents every [update_time_in_seconds] seconds -rm [ID] -> remove this RSS feed -ls -> open your RSS feed list; tap a feed to edit it -l [ID] -> show the whole content of the corresponding RSS feed -show [ID] [boolean] -> toggle the [show] property of the given saved RSS feed -update_time [ID] [update_time_in_seconds] -> set the update time of the corresponding RSS feed -url [ID] [url] -> update the URL of the corresponding RSS feed -alias [ID] [alias] -> rename the corresponding RSS feed in lists and modules -format [ID] [format] -> set the format of the corresponding RSS feed ([format] can be both a string or the ID of an existing format) -color [ID] [color] -> set the base color of the corresponding RSS feed -wifi_only [ID] [boolean] -> if [boolean] is true, the corresponding feed will be updated only if your device is connected to a WiFi network -last_check [ID] -> show the last time Re:T-UI checked this RSS feed -entry_tag [ID] -> set the base tag for every single entry (default: "item") -date_tag [ID] [tag] -> set the tag which holds info about the publication date (default: "pubDate") -add_command [ID] [IDs (comma separated)] [regex] [cmd] -> create a new regex command that will be applied on the RSS feeds corresponding to IDs -rm_command [ID] -> rm the corresponding regex command -frc [ID] -> update the corresponding RSS feed -info [ID] -> show info about the corresponding RSS feed settings -include_if_matches [ID] [regex] -> if the given regex matches on an RSS feed item, it will be shown ([regex] can be both a string or the ID of a regex saved inside regex.xml) -exclude_if_matches [ID] [regex] -> if the given regex matches on an RSS feed item, it won't be shown ([regex] can be both a string or the ID of a regex saved inside regex.xml) -add_format [ID] [format] -> create a new format that you will be able to use for more than one RSS feed -rm_format [ID] [format] -> remove an existing format -file -> open the file rss.xml
Reddit/module example: $ rss -add 1 900 https://www.reddit.com/r/android/.rss $ rss -frc 1 $ module -dock add rss $ module -show rss
